newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shares fall sharply on Wall Street loss.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shares fall sharply on Wall Street loss.

text.p: Israeli shares closed sharply lower on Sunday in thin trading in response to the decline of Israeli shares traded in New York on Friday, traders said.

The benchmark Mishtanim index of top 100 shares fell 2.86 percent, or 7.23 points, to 245.91 on low all-share turnover of 132 million shekels against 127 million shekels on Thursday, the last day of trading before the Israeli weekend.
The Maof 25 blue chip index closed 2.67 percent lower at 254.38.

"The decline of Israeli stocks traded in New York had a negative impact on trading today and the market closed lower led by a sharp decline in small capitalisation stocks traded on the Karam," said Ari Eidelheit of Zeler Eblagon Securities.
"The nervousness of Wall Street is worrying. I believe that the correction will continue one or two more days," said Danni Scharia of Capital Securities.
But analyst said the recent downturn was only a correction and not a trend in trend.
"The market rose sharply after October with no real consolidation. I believe that the Maof will stabilise at 250 before it starts rising again," Eidelheit said.

"The market rose sharply than it lost almost 10 percent and now it is looking for a new equilibrium. The fact that the market continues to decline on low turnover indicates that this only a correction and not a negative trend," Scharia added.

The most active shares were Koor Industries, which fell 3.75 percent to 30,993 agorot on turnover of 7.0 million shekels; Teva Pharmaceutical Industries, which lost 2.25 percent to 20,631 agorot on volume of 6.9 million shekels; and Israel Chemicals, which fell 2.5 percent to 365 agorot on turnover of 5.9 million shekels.
